case.pattern_description: The fraud pattern involves five online transactions totaling $1,904.86, with each transaction just under $500, all within a 30-minute window on a single card. This pattern was found by scanning the card's transaction history, revealing a sequence of transactions that matched five previously confirmed but unmapped cases. The fraud affects cardholders whose cards are used in this manner, and it was identified by an agent who noticed recurring bursts of transactions in the same region and timeframe.

sar.narrative: Customer C02265, holder of card C02265-K1, is the subject of this report. Between 2016-12-02 19:00 and 2016-12-02 19:30, 4 transaction(s) totalling $1,904.86 were made on the card online from device profile 'Windows | Windows 10 | chrome 64.0 | 1920x1080': $481.66 (3507563, 2016-12-02 19:00), $468.32 (3507591, 2016-12-02 19:08), $485.41 (3507626, 2016-12-02 19:20), $469.47 (3507670, 2016-12-02 19:30). Every amount sat just below $500 and the purchases were placed minutes apart, a pattern consistent with deliberately staying under an authorisation threshold. The activity is suspicious because: 4 online purchases within 30 minutes, each between $400 and $500 ($481.66, $468.32, $485.41, $469.47; total $1,904.86). It closely resembles earlier confirmed fraud cases CC-3748, CC-3841, CC-3907. The bank has recommended blocking and reissuing the card, placing linked cards under monitoring where applicable, and retains the transaction, device and investigation records as supporting documentation.
